chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Burayd ibn Mu'awiya, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying regarding Al-Ila' (oath of abstention from wife): When a man takes an oath not to approach his wife, nor touch her, nor join his head with her head, he is in ease (has time) as long as four months do not pass. When four months have passed and he is asked (to choose), either he returns (to intimacy) and touches her, or he resolves on divorce, so he frees her until she menstruates and purifies from her menses, then he divorces her with one pronouncement before he has intercourse with her, with the testimony of two just witnesses. Then he is more entitled to take her back as long as the three menstrual periods have not passed.

key_terms.الرَّجْعَةِ: Revocation of divorce; taking the wife back during the waiting period
key_terms.الْإِيلَاءِ: Oath of abstaining from sexual intercourse with one's wife
key_terms.يُقَامَ: To be asked or put to a choice (in legal context)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling and procedure for Al-Ila (oath of abstention) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith clarifies that the forced divorce resulting from 'Ila' is classified as a revocable divorce (Taliqat Raj'iyya), distinguishing it from the final divorce. It emphasizes the procedural requirement of a single pronouncement during a period of purity (Tuhr) before consummation, ensuring the husband retains the right of return (Ruj'u) within the three menstrual cycles, thereby preserving the marital bond's potential for reconciliation.
